try: Lay out Sophia’s schedule from her signed quote
how:
1. Open Sophia’s project; on its Overview read "Needs you", then press "Set up" on the "Schedule" row
2. Read "Works start on", "Milestones come from" and "What you will get"
3. Pick "A schedule template", look at the drawing, then pick "A quote" again
expect: Needs you lists "The Deposit invoice is ready to send", "Schedule" and "Invite the client" (the filled button reads "Send the Deposit invoice"). "Set up" opens the Schedule tab on "Set up the schedule"; works start on her start date. "A quote" says "One milestone for each stage of work in OM-…, in the order it runs on site …". What you will get lists each stage with its dates, "Handover around …, n weeks after works start." and "Payments follow the quote: 10% deposit, 30% commencement, …". The template redraws it.
in10: Different from 1.0: built from the quote, shown before it is made

try: Create her schedule and read it
how:
1. Press "Create schedule"
2. Read the top of the tab, the rows, and the line beside the eye with the button next to it
3. Read the sentences under the list
expect: "Schedule set up". One list that is also the timeline: names on the left, a bar per milestone to scale, weekends shaded, today’s line, a diamond where a payment falls due. The top sums up Done · To handover · Next payment. Beside the eye: "Sophia has no portal yet — invite them to see the schedule." and an outlined "Share the schedule"; the filled button still reads "Send the Deposit invoice".
in10: Different from 1.0: list and timeline are one

how:
1. Press "Months", then "Weeks"
2. Scroll the bars sideways, then press "Today"
expect: Months squeezes the job onto the screen, Weeks spreads it out with week heads; Today brings today’s line back to the middle.

how:
1. Open Benjamin Han’s project › "Schedule"
2. Read the top, then the line beside the eye and the button next to it
3. Read each row’s grey line
expect: The top reads "Handover moves to …, one week later." with "Carpentry now ends …. Painting, cleaning and handover moved with it."; Done 3 of 7. The eye line says "Benjamin still sees the schedule shared on …, handover …" (a week before the new one) and "4 changes to share.", with an outlined "Share 4 changes" beside it. Four rows wear "+1 week" with a dashed outline where he last saw them; Painting is striped amber: "Waiting on Benjamin for paint colours · n days". (The demo’s dates move with the day you reset it, every gap kept — so these steps name the gaps, not the days.)

try: See the schedule as Benjamin has it now
how:
1. Press the eye line
2. Compare the pane with the list
3. Close the pane
expect: A pane "What Benjamin sees", "Shared …, handover …", shows his copy: Carpentry still ending a week earlier and the handover a week earlier, with the studio’s note; its foot says "Changes reach Benjamin only when you share them."

try: Move a milestone and take it back
how:
1. Drag the "Carpentry fabrication" bar a few days to the right, watching the dates over it
2. Let go and read the message
3. Press "Undo"
expect: Dates show over the bar as it moves ("… – …") and the milestones after it move along, ringed. On release: "Carpentry moved n days later. 3 milestones followed. n open tasks moved with them." with Undo; Undo puts every date back.
in10: Different from 1.0: what follows moves too, and says so

try: Change only the end, or change your mind mid-drag
how:
1. Start dragging the Carpentry bar again and press Esc before letting go
2. Drag the bar’s right end one day to the right and let go
3. Press "Undo"
expect: Esc puts the bar back with no message. The end drag says "Carpentry now ends …, 1 day later. 3 milestones followed. n open tasks moved with them." with Undo; Undo puts it back.

try: Move a bar from the keyboard
how:
1. Press Tab until the Carpentry bar is outlined
2. Press → twice and wait a moment
3. Press ⌘Z (Ctrl+Z)
4. Press ?, read "A project’s schedule", press Esc
expect: Each → moves it a day; the two presses land as one move with its sentence, and ⌘Z presses its Undo. The ? list has "A project’s schedule": Move it a day earlier · later, Move it a week, Its last day…, Open the focused bar, Put a moving bar back.

try: Open a milestone and read its layers
how:
1. Click the "Painting" bar without dragging
2. Read the panel from top to bottom
3. Press "Cancel"
expect: A panel "Painting": the status (Not started · In progress · Blocked · Done); When — Starts, Ends, "10 days. Push it later by 1 day · 3 days · 1 week", "Moves with" and "If carpentry moves, painting moves by the same number of days.", "1 week later than first shared (…)."; Tasks (three); switches "Shown to Benjamin", "Waiting on someone" (Benjamin, paint colours), "A payment falls due here", "Ask Benjamin to confirm it".
in10: Different from 1.0: one panel; waits, payments and the client in it

how:
1. Read the grey lines of "Masonry & tiling" and "Electrical & plumbing"
2. Open "Masonry & tiling", read the end of the panel, press "Cancel"
3. Open "Electrical & plumbing", read "Ask Benjamin to confirm it", press "Cancel"
expect: The rows read "Shared … · Benjamin confirmed it …" (the next day) and "Shared … · waiting for Benjamin to confirm". Masonry’s panel shows "Benjamin confirmed it · …" in green; Electrical’s says "Waiting for Benjamin to confirm it on their portal."
in10: Different from 1.0: the client confirms only when asked

try: Add a task inside a milestone
how:
1. Open "Painting", press "Add a task", type Buy sample pots for the living room, press Enter
2. Press "Cancel" to close the panel
3. Open the "Tasks" tab (it opens on "All tasks") and find the task
expect: "Task added to Painting" — due on Painting’s last day, with the project’s team on it. On Tasks a "Milestone" column after Title reads "Painting"; Filters has a "Milestone" tab with "In no milestone".
in10: Different from 1.0: tasks live inside milestones

try: Read a late job and mark a stage done
how:
1. Open Ryan D’Souza’s project › "Schedule"; read the top and the "Electrical & plumbing" row
2. On that row press "Mark done" and read the sheet: "When", "Tell Ryan", "Money"
3. Untick "Show it on Ryan’s schedule as done" and "Send the Mid-Project invoice", then press "Mark done"
4. Press "Undo"
expect: The top is red: "2 milestones are late. Handover is set for …."; Electrical’s line reads "Blocked · waiting on the plumber … · was due …, n days late". The sheet "Mark Electrical & plumbing done" says "… late — it was due to end …"; under Money "Send the Mid-Project invoice · S$…" is ticked. Then "Electrical marked done." with Undo; Undo answers "Electrical is back as it was" — Blocked and late again.
in10: Different from 1.0: late stages say so in words

try: Get reminded when a milestone ends or runs late
how:
1. "Demo Studio" block › "View as" › "Michelle"
2. Click the bell (Notifications) and read the "Due" rows
3. Press "Overdue: Electrical & plumbing"
4. "View as" › "Dane"
expect: Michelle’s bell has "Overdue: Electrical & plumbing" and "Overdue: Carpentry fabrication" (Executive Condo — Ryan D’Souza, n days late) — and "Ends in n days: …" when a milestone ends within three days; the row opens the milestone on Ryan’s schedule.
in10: Different from 1.0: reminders come whether the timeline is open or not

try: Share the new dates with Benjamin
how:
1. Back as Dane, open Benjamin Han’s project › "Schedule" and press "Share 4 changes" beside the eye line
2. Read "What changes for Benjamin" and "What Benjamin will see"
3. In "A note for Benjamin (optional)" type Carpentry needs one more week for the wardrobes.
4. Press "Share 4 changes"
expect: "Share changes with Benjamin" strikes each old date beside the new one, a week later (Carpentry’s end … Handover); the right shows his copy with "Updated … · Handover is now …" and your note. Then "Shared 4 changes with Benjamin" (leave its "Tell Benjamin on WhatsApp"); the line reads "Benjamin sees this schedule. Last shared …"; the +1 week marks and the "Share 4 changes" button go.
in10: Different from 1.0: nothing reaches the client until you share it

try: Share Sophia’s schedule for the first time
how:
1. Open Sophia’s project › "Schedule" and press "Share the schedule" beside the eye line
2. Read the window, then press "Share the schedule"
expect: The window is "Share the schedule with Sophia": "Sophia has no portal yet — the schedule is kept for them, and they see it once you invite them."; "What Sophia will get" says she hasn’t seen the schedule yet and that sharing sends the n milestones shown to her, with the handover day. Then "Schedule kept for Sophia — they see it once you invite them" — leave its "Invite Sophia": chapter 19 invites her.

try: Keep Benjamin’s schedule as a template
how:
1. On Benjamin’s Schedule open ⋮ ("More for the schedule") › "Save as a template"
2. Keep the name "Benjamin Han’s schedule", press "Save"
3. Press "Open" in the message
expect: "Saved to Company › Templates › Schedules" with Open; Open opens "Benjamin Han’s schedule" in the schedule template editor, under the crumbs Company / Templates / Schedules.

how:
1. Press "Schedules" in the crumbs above the name; read the cards and the "New" menu
2. Open "Whole-home renovation (HDB)"
3. Read the columns and "How it lays out", then press "Done"
expect: Cards draw their milestones to scale: "Whole-home renovation (HDB)" (7 milestones · 12 weeks), "Kitchen and bathroom refresh" (5 milestones · 4 weeks), Benjamin Han’s, and five "Ready-made · …" (HDB BTO, HDB resale, Condo, Landed, Commercial fit-out). New offers "Start from a whole-home renovation", a "Ready-made: …" for each, and "Blank schedule". The editor lists Milestone · Days · Gap (days) · Client confirms, with "How it lays out" beneath.

how:
1. "Settings" › "Projects", scroll to the "Schedule" card
2. Under "Where a schedule starts, by project type" set "Studio default" to Whole-home renovation (HDB)
3. Set it back to "The signed quote’s stages"
expect: Each pick saves at once, with Undo: "The studio default is now Whole-home renovation (HDB)", then "The studio default is now the signed quote’s stages". The project types below read "Same as the studio default"; the card’s approvals now sit in "What waits for an Owner or an Admin", at the top.

try: Check a schedule on your phone
how:
1. On your phone open Benjamin Han’s project › "Schedule"
2. Tap the "Painting" row, then close the sheet
3. Tap "Done" on the "Carpentry fabrication" row, read the sheet, then "Cancel"
expect: The top reads "n days to go · 3 of 7 done"; each row has a thin bar to scale with today’s line, and each not done its own "Done". A row opens its milestone as a bottom sheet; Done opens "Mark Carpentry fabrication done" from the bottom. "Add milestone" sits at the foot — on Schedule it takes the place of the bar Photos · Done · Note · Message. Dates move in the sheet, not by dragging.
in10: Different from 1.0: the schedule works on a phone
